Recursively collapse the JSON array-of-one vs scalar ambiguity

Source: R/stac_helpers.R
normalize_stac_scalars.Rd

write_stac() writes with auto_unbox = TRUE, so an unnamed length-1 list like list("data") (e.g. an asset's roles) is written as the bare JSON string "data", not the array ["data"]. Reading that file back via read_stac() therefore yields a plain scalar, not a length-1 list - even though nothing about the actual content changed. Every change-detection comparison in this package runs both sides through this (alongside strip_fs_path()) so a freshly-built object (with e.g. roles = list("data")) compares equal to its round-tripped disk version (roles = "data").

Usage

normalize_stac_scalars(x)

Arguments

x

Any R object (typically a STAC list structure)

Value

The same structure with unnamed length-1 lists of an atomic scalar collapsed to that scalar
